content.title: Paris-Roubaix: Everything you need to know about the Hell of the North
content.text: Date: Sunday, April 12, 2026Start: Denian (women) and Compiègne (men)Finish: Roubaix Total distance: 148.5km (women) and 259.2km (men)Defending champion: Pauline Ferrand-Prévot (Visma-Lease a Bike) and Mathieu van der Poel (Alpecin-Decuninck) Paris-Roubaix has been nicknamed the Hell of the North, a Sunday in Hell and the Queen of the Classics in its past. The parcours are brutal and often leave riders covered in dust, mud, and grit alongside their sweat and tears (and frequently blood) as one of the toughest races to finish in all of cycling. The reputation of the race is such that just reaching the velodrome within the time limit can be the highlight of a rider's career. At the same time, some are lucky enough to take a podium or a victory and etch their name in the history of cycling forever. Of course, some transcend the abilities of an average rider and garner multiple victories throughout their careers. That illustrious list includes household names like Rik Van Looy, Eddy Merckx, Roger De Vlaeminck, Francesco Moser, Sean Kelly, Johan Museeuw, Tom Boonen, Fabian Cancellara, and Mathieu van der Poel among others. De Vlaeminck and Boonen are perhaps the finest over the French cobbles, each arriving at the famous Roubaix Velodrome as champion on a record four occasions. It is the Belgians who have been the best at Roubaix for men throughout the race’s history, with a total of 57 wins and six separate riders winning the fabled Monument three or more times. Despite this, the Belgian's last victory was in 2019 when Philippe Gilbert took the spoils. The Dutch have dominated the race recently, with Van der Poel winning the past three editions of the race and Dylan van Baarle taking the 2022 title. Van der Poel is confirmed to be back on the start line in 2026 in search of a fourth victory in a row – a feat never achieved previously. However, he has a stacked field to race against, including his long-time rival, Wout van Aert, who is vying for a win on the cobbles and on eof the greatest ever Tadej Pogačar. Pogačar made his debut in 2025 and pushed Van der Poel for much of the race only to crash and lose time. The Slovenian world champion is back in 2026 to try and win the Queen of the Classics. Biniam Girmay, Tim Merlier, Arnaud De Lie, Josh Tarling and Mads Pedersen are also making their way to Compiègne in an attempt to add a Monument title to their palmarès. Men's Paris-Roubaix 2026 team list: Ineos GrenadiersXDS Astana TeamBahrain-Victorous Jayco AlUlaPicnic PostNLMovistar Groupama-FDJ Lidl-TrekIntermarché-Wanty EF Education-EasyPostVisma-Lease a BikeArké-B&B HotelsAlpecin-DeceuninckCofidisSoudal–Quick-StepUAE Team Emirates-XRGRed Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe Decathlon AG2R MondialeLottoUno-X Mobility Israel-Premier TechQ36.5 Cycling TeamTeam TotalEnergiesTudor Pro CyclingUnibet Tietema Rockets Men's Paris-Roubaix 2026 route: For 2026, the men’s route has seen some slight alterations, which include one more sector of bone-jarring cobbles and a different approach to the Trouée d’Arenberg. Other than those alterations, the men’s route is of similar distance to last year’s at 259.2 kilometres and starts in Compiègne and finishes in Roubaix. The first cobbled sector, after the village of Troisvilles into Inchy, is tackled 100km into the race. From then on, the sections come thick and fast, with several challenging cobbled sections for the riders to contend with. However, it is the hotly anticipated Trouée d’Arenberg that arrives after 11 cobbled sections and will span 2.3km with uneven, jarring cobblestones. In the lead-up to the Forest of Arenberg, there have been some changes, including the tight chicane, added to the race last minute in 2024 after many riders expressed concerns about the high speed entering the section on a straight road. For 2025, the organisers have added four right-hand corners in the kilometre before section 19, which aims to slow down the riders in the approach. The other changes made by the organisers for this year are two new cobbled sections 30km before the Arenberg. Sections 23 and 24 – Famars (1.2km) and Artres (1.3km) – are both new to the race and are included in a small loop around the municipality of Quérénaing, aimed at increasing the intensity of the race in the approach to the Arenberg. These are the only changes which have been made to the race for this year, however. Fan favourites resume after the Arenberg, with the Mons-en-Pévèl section (3km) and the Carrefour de l’Arbre (2.1km) coming shortly after. The Carrefour de l’Arbre is the third from the last section of cobblestones before the shorter section, which is in the approach to the famous velodrome, where the riders will complete a lap-and-a-half on the wooden boards. Paris-Roubaix Femmes Avec Zwift The women’s peloton had to see 117 editions of the men's race go by before they got their chance to race on the pavé. The sixth edition of Paris-Roubaix Femmes avec Zwift will be held on Sunday, April 12, 2026. The women’s peloton will complete a similar but shorter route to the men, including the five-star sectors Mons-en–Pévèle and Carrefour de l’Arbre. The women’s race has a short history in which Lidl-Trek have dominated with two solo wins – Lizzie Deignan in the inaugural edition and Elisa Longo Borghini in 2022 – but Alison Jackson (EF Education-Cannondale) broke the Lidl-Trek winning streak in 2023 after an unlikely breakaway win, which saw the Canadian rider hold the iconic Roubaix cobblestone above her head. Then, Lotte Kopecky (SD Worx-Protime) in 2024 in a sprint against Elisa Balsamo (Lidl-Trek), Pfeiffer Georgi (dsm-firmenich PostNL), Marianne Vos (Visma-Lease a Bike), and Amber Kraak (FDJ-Suez). Last year Pauline Ferrand-Prévot became the first Frenchwoman to win France's Monument in what was a glorious double in 2025 with Tour de France Femmes avec Zwift victory coming later in the season. Paris-Roubaix Femmes avec Zwift 2026 teams: FDJ-SuezLidl-TrekMovistarCanyon//SRAM zondacryptoAG Insurance-Soudal TeamVisma-Lease a BikeSD Worx-ProtimeWinspace Orange Seal Ceratizit Pro CyclingFenix-DeceuninckHuman Powered Health Liv AlUla JaycoRolandPicnic PostNL UAE Team ADQUno-X MobilityAkéa-B&B HotelsCofidis Women TeamEF Education-OatlySt Michel-Preference Home-Auber93VolkerWessels Women’s Pro CyclingDD Group Pro CyclingLotto LadiesTeam Coop-Repsol Paris-Roubaix Femmes avec Zwift 2026 route: The women’s route has not been changed for 2026 and will follow the same route as the previous edition, remaining at 148.5 kilometres in length and covering 29.2km of pavé. The race will begin in Denian and finish in the iconic Roubaix Velodrome to crown its fifth winner of the gruelling race. It takes in 17 sectors of cobbles, including the five-star sectors Mons-en-Pévèl and the Carrefour de l’Arbre. However, it does not include the infamous Trouée d’Arenberg – fortunately for the riders, not so fortunately for the spectators. Similar to the men’s race, once the women’s peloton reaches the prestigious velodrome, they will complete the traditional lap-and-a-half before the winner can lift the iconic Paris-Roubaix cobble above their head.
